此工作流程专为 LTX 2.3 四图像参考视频生成而设计，允许创作者从多个视觉参考构建连续的电影视频，而不是仅仅依赖单个图像或文本提示。其主要目的是使用四张参考图像作为场景设计、角色外观、产品细节、氛围和动作连续性的视觉锚点，然后生成对身份、环境和视觉逻辑具有更强控制力的连贯的LTX 2.3视频。

该工作流程使用 LTX 2.3 Dev-Dare 合并的蒸馏组件作为主要视频生成主干，以及 Gemma 3 文本编码、LTX 音频/视频潜在路由、LTX 视频 VAE 解码和自定义采样器结构。它还包括 LTX2.3 CrispEnhance 和 VBVR I2V 式 LoRA 支持等增强路线，使其更适合视觉一致性很重要的受控图像到视频生成。

主要特点是多参考指南结构。可以分别加载和处理四个图像，然后通过 ImageResizeKJv2 和 LTXVPreprocess 调整大小和准备。这些引用通过 LTXVAddGuideMulti 注入到生成过程中。这为模型提供了不止一种可以遵循的视觉源。一张图像可以定义主要主题，另一张图像可以定义产品，另一张图像可以提供场景或灯光氛围，另一张图像可以指导最终的视觉风格或氛围。

该工作流程还使用 PromptRelayEncodeTimeline，这对于视频控制很重要。工作流程可以将视频描述为基于时间的序列，而不是只编写一个静态提示。全局提示定义了整体场景、主题、氛围和视觉规则，而局部提示描述了不同时间段发生的事情。这使得最终视频更具电影感且更少随机性，因为该模型同时接收到稳定的视觉概念和清晰的时间方向。

在上传的设置中，工作流程是围绕精美的美容产品展示构建的。提示描述了一位年轻的东亚女性在干净的工作室或电影环境中展示蓝色护肤精华液瓶，镜头移动受控，光线柔和，产品可见度高，角色表演稳定。这显示了工作流程的预期强度：它不仅适用于抽象动画，还适用于商业风格的视频生成、产品演示、AI影响者剪辑、时尚预览和短片广告内容。

该工作流程包括多个采样和细化阶段、手动 sigma 控制、NAG 增强、潜在升级、平铺 VAE 解码和最终视频导出。这些部分有助于改进细节、减少偏差并使输出更适合发布。最终结果可以通过视频合并路径导出为视频，以便为 RunningHub 演示、Civita 预览、YouTube 展示和 Bilibili 发布做好准备。

简而言之，这是一个实用的四图像参考 LTX 2.3 视频工作流程，适合想要更强的视觉控制、更好的参考融合和更稳定的影院视频输出的创作者。如果您想了解四个参考图像如何连接、PromptRelay 如何控制时间线以及如何生成最终视频，请从上面的 YouTube 链接观看完整教程。

o.en:
This workflow is designed for LTX 2.3 four-image reference video generation, allowing creators to build a continuous cinematic video from multiple visual references instead of relying on a single image or a text prompt alone. Its main purpose is to use four reference images as visual anchors for scene design, character appearance, product details, atmosphere, and motion continuity, then generate a coherent LTX 2.3 video with stronger control over identity, environment, and visual logic.

The workflow uses LTX 2.3 Dev-Dare merged distilled components as the main video generation backbone, together with Gemma 3 text encoding, LTX audio / video latent routing, LTX video VAE decoding, and a custom sampler structure. It also includes enhancement routes such as LTX2.3 Crisp Enhance and VBVR I2V-style LoRA support, making it more suitable for controlled image-to-video generation where visual consistency matters.

The key feature is the multi-reference guide structure. Four images can be loaded and processed separately, then resized and prepared through ImageResizeKJv2 and LTXVPreprocess. These references are injected into the generation process through LTXVAddGuideMulti. This gives the model more than one visual source to follow. One image can define the main subject, another can define the product, another can provide the scene or lighting mood, and another can guide the final visual style or atmosphere.

The workflow also uses PromptRelayEncodeTimeline, which is important for video control. Instead of writing only one static prompt, the workflow can describe the video as a time-based sequence. The global prompt defines the overall scene, subject, atmosphere, and visual rules, while local prompts describe what happens in different time segments. This makes the final video more cinematic and less random, because the model receives both a stable visual concept and a clear temporal direction.

In the uploaded setup, the workflow is structured around a polished beauty product showcase. The prompt describes a young adult East Asian woman presenting a blue skincare serum bottle in a clean studio or cinematic environment, with controlled camera movement, soft light, product visibility, and stable character performance. This shows the intended strength of the workflow: it is not only for abstract animation, but also for commercial-style video generation, product demonstration, AI influencer clips, fashion previews, and short-form advertising content.

The workflow includes multiple sampling and refinement stages, manual sigma control, NAG enhancement, latent upscaling, tiled VAE decoding, and final video export. These sections help improve detail, reduce drift, and make the output more usable for publishing. The final result can be exported as a video through the video combine route, making it ready for RunningHub demos, Civitai previews, YouTube showcases, and Bilibili publishing.

In short, this is a practical four-image reference LTX 2.3 video workflow for creators who want stronger visual control, better reference fusion, and more stable cinematic video output. If you want to see how the four reference images are connected, how PromptRelay controls the timeline, and how the final video is generated, watch the full tutorial from the YouTube link above.
